description: Individual entries for twelve major aerial environmental hazards.

entries.title: Lightning Storm
entries.summary: Violent electrical storms strike sails, exposed equipment, passengers, and magical ship systems without warning.
body: Static-heavy air and repeated bolts can ignite fires, disable controls, and force crews to divide attention between piloting and damage control.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Pilot checks and lightning-damage values require conversion.

entries.title: Turbulent Winds
entries.summary: Erratic currents throw vessels from course, reduce altitude, and drive them toward nearby obstacles.
body: Turbulence becomes especially dangerous to damaged ships, loose cargo, separated fleets, and crews already struggling with morale or fatigue.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Piloting checks, altitude loss, and collision damage require conversion.

entries.title: Toxic Fog
entries.summary: Poisonous low-visibility clouds cause confusion, nausea, respiratory injury, and unconsciousness.
body: Fog hides terrain and vessels while harmful vapors accumulate through prolonged exposure. Filters, sealed compartments, route changes, and rapid extraction are critical.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Saving throws, poison duration, and damage require conversion.

entries.title: Gravity Anomaly
entries.summary: Sudden directional gravity shifts pull creatures, cargo, islands, and ships toward unexpected surfaces or the Abyss.
body: A vessel may roll, collide, or lose crew before pilots understand which direction has become down. Secured cargo and tethered sailors survive anomalies more reliably.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Saving throws, random movement, impact, and falling damage require conversion.

entries.title: Skyquake
entries.summary: Tremors ripple through air and floating terrain, breaking islands apart and filling routes with debris.
body: Skyquakes destabilize lift, alignment, settlements, docks, and nearby vessels. Secondary debris storms can continue after the initial disturbance.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Piloting checks, altitude loss, and debris damage require conversion.

entries.title: Magical Null Zone
entries.summary: Patches of sky suppress spells, enchantments, magical devices, and magically powered flight.
body: Ships dependent on arcane propulsion may immediately begin falling or drifting. Crews need nonmagical redundancy, rapid diagnosis, and a route out before lift or life-support systems fail.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Arcana checks and the source's fixed suppression duration require conversion.

entries.title: Solar Flare
entries.summary: Bursts of radiation and glare overheat hulls, ignite fires, blind pilots, and disrupt magical energy.
body: Delicate equipment and exposed crews are particularly vulnerable. Heat management and alternate navigation become as important as avoiding direct structural damage.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Fire damage and navigation penalties require conversion.

entries.title: Raging Winds of the Abyss
entries.summary: Violent downward currents drag vessels toward lower clouds, debris, and the edge of the Abyss.
body: The winds oppose escape and can turn a navigational error into an accelerating descent. Strong propulsion, coordinated piloting, and early route correction are essential.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Opposed piloting checks and collision damage require conversion.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Environmental Hazards / Raging Winds of the Abyss

entries.title: Mystic Rain
entries.summary: Rare acidic or magical rain corrodes hulls, weakens structures, drains enchanted equipment, and attracts magical creatures.
body: The event can appear beneficial or beautiful before its corrosive effects become clear. Covered equipment, sealed cargo, and rapid maintenance reduce permanent losses.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Acid damage and permanent charge-loss values require conversion.

entries.title: Tornado of the Skies
entries.summary: A rotating funnel of wind, debris, and magical energy can seize and shred entire airships.
body: The vortex cuts through routes like a moving blade, throwing survivors and wreckage great distances. Avoidance is safer than attempting to cross its path.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Piloting checks, damage, and throw distance require conversion.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Environmental Hazards / Tornado of the Skies

entries.title: Whispering Winds
entries.summary: Voices carried in strange winds produce hallucinations, vertigo, confusion, and false navigation cues.
body: Crews may misread routes, separate, or take random action while convinced the whispers are warnings or instructions. Shared navigation checks and isolation from the sound reduce danger.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Wisdom checks and confusion duration require conversion.

entries.title: Sky Miasma
entries.summary: Dark toxic cloud fields drain vitality and progressively slow ships and living creatures.
body: The miasma turns prolonged passage into a contest of endurance. Engines, crews, and animals all become sluggish as exposure accumulates and ordinary work grows difficult.

sections.heading: Legacy Hazard Procedure
body: Exhaustion timing and check penalties require conversion.
